newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen plans to ban citizens from carrying weapons.
newsitem.headline: Yemen plans to ban citizens from carrying weapons.

text.p: Yemen plans to ban citizens from carrying weapons in the streets under a new law that will consider such an act a crime, the interior minister said on Wednesday.

The move, after weeks of a disarmament campaign, will help stem "the continued phenomenon of taking revenge... which is harming the country's reputation," Hussein Mohammad Arab told state-run television.
"The present law does not consider carrying (even licensed) weapons or opening fire in the cities an offence," he said.
"A new law will be submitted to parliament and will consider carrying weapons and using them illegally a crime that will be accounted for".

Arab said an attempt to collect a vast arsenal of unlicensed weapons in April, before the Arab state's first parliamentary elections since a 1994 civil war nearly tore Yemen apart, was hampered by the existing law on firearms.
"In our campaign to collect weapons, we were seizing between 500 to 600 pieces of arms a day but we had to return them to their owners because the old law did not ban this".
The move in April came weeks after a gunman shot dead four children and two teachers at adjacent schools in Sanaa. The assailant was executed in public.
The shooting spree shocked and enraged the nation, with newspapers calling for steps to cut down on the proliferation of unlicensed weapons.
Illicit guns, mainly Kalashnikov automatic rifles, are openly carried in Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest countries.
Unofficial estimates put the number of firearms at nearly 50 million, three times the population of 16 million.
